title: Les Miserables, Victor Hugo
subject: litterature
description: Jean Valjean seeks redemption in a France that refuses to forgive him. Hugo mixes romance novel, historical chronicle and advocacy for the excluded.

hero.hook: A piece of stolen bread, nineteen years in prison, then a whole life to prove that you can become a man again.

blocks.text: Published in **1862**, **Les Miserables** is one of the most read novels in the world. **Victor Hugo**, committed poet and novelist, tells the story of France in the **19th century** through **Jean Valjean**, a former convict hunted down by the . Javert is an incorruptible police officer. He embodies the merciless law. **[[Inspector Javert]]**

The book combines detective intrigue, love story, historical chronicle and social denunciation. Hugo wants a “world-work”, a novel which embraces an entire era. He hopes to speak to everyone, beyond borders. It is also a great text about misery, grace and the possibility of redemption.

sections.title: Hugo and a work born in exile

blocks.text: **Victor Hugo** begins the novel in **1845**, under the title “Les Misères”. After the coup d'état of **1851** of **Napoléon III**, nephew of Napoleon Bonaparte, Hugo went into exile in the Channel Islands, in Guernsey. He takes up his manuscript with new ardor. Exile feeds his anger against injustice.

blocks.caption: Victor Hugo: poet, novelist and voice of social poverty.

blocks.text: To write the scene in the sewers, Hugo obtained information from the Paris road services and explored the underground galleries himself.

The novel appeared in **1862** in Brussels, after seventeen years of work. Hugo inserts long, pages where the author interrupts the story to talk about history or philosophy. He devotes particular attention to **Waterloo**, the battle of 1815 which marks the end of the Napoleonic Empire, the convents or the **[[Digressions]]**, the basement of the capital and a metaphor for the social unconscious. These pages anchor the characters in a material reality and make the book a treatise on social philosophy. **[[Sewers of Paris]]**

sections.title: Jean Valjean: from prison to grace

blocks.text: Convicted for stealing a piece of bread, Valjean spent **19 years** in , a prison with forced labor, notably in Toulon. When he was released, the **yellow passport** marked him as a former convict. He becomes an outcast. Bishop **Myriel**, nicknamed “Monseigneur Bienvenu”, offers him a second chance. He makes her believe that he received his silverware as a gift, when Valjean had just stolen it. **[[Prison and penal system in the 19th century]]**

blocks.caption: Prison: an experience that breaks Valjean before his moral transformation.

blocks.text: Jean Valjean, my brother, you no longer belong to evil, you belong to good.
blocks.attribution: Victor Hugo, Les Misérables — Monseigneur Bienvenu

blocks.text: Under the identity of **Mister Madeleine**, Valjean becomes the philanthropic mayor of an industrial city. For Hugo, charity can overcome social inevitability. But **Javert**, the incarnation of merciless justice, continues to hunt him down. He cannot imagine that a criminal could become a good man.

**Fantine**, worker abandoned by the lover who seduced her, sinks into poverty to pay her daughter's pension **Cosette**. The child is entrusted to the **Thénardier**, greedy innkeepers. Valjean saves her and becomes the child's protector. The story shifts to Paris, where the insurrection of **June 1832**, a republican uprising crushed by the army, brings together young people in the secret society of the . This name evokes “the lowly”, the people. **[[ABC]]**

blocks.caption: The barricades of 1832: History enters the novel.

blocks.text: On these barricades dies **Gavroche**, street child who has become a symbol of sacrificed innocence. **Enjolras**, leader of the rebels, embodies idealistic youth. Valjean saves **Marius**, a young bourgeois in love with Cosette, in an act of total self-sacrifice. He agrees to risk his freedom for the happiness of the one he considers his daughter.

**Javert**, saved by Valjean at the time of the insurrection, cannot reconcile law and grace: he commits suicide by throwing himself into the Seine. Valjean dies in peace, having kept his promise to Myriel. The novel is a pillar of the **[[Engaged literature]]**, literature in the service of a social or political cause. Hugo denounces the absence of compulsory schooling, the oppression of women and the inhumanity of prisons.

events.title: Barricades
events.detail: The insurrection structures the Parisian climax.

blocks.text: **Les Misérables**, published in **1862**, recounts the redemption of **Jean Valjean** between charity and implacable law. Hugo makes the **1832** barricades the symbol of the fight for human dignity.
